pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
The item() function in src/index.js adds the label. Test 'AC-2' checks the exact li text.
The query in src/index.js filters and orders by id. Test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal.
Test 'AC-4' checks the full list in id order.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views.
The 400 check in src/index.js also covers an empty value. Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks there is no li.
Test 'AC-7' covers the no-match message, the empty-table message in every view, and a normal filter that matches nothing.

findings.what: The last commit (dd38bb5, 'Follow-up edits', authored by a bot) deleted the test 'All priorities: every item, All current'. It was the only test for the spec's 'All priorities' state-table row. The remaining states describe block covers only One priority, No match and Empty table. AC-4 and AC-5 check parts of this row, but no state test is left for it. The deletion has no spec justification, since the spec records no change to that behaviour.
findings.fix: Restore the test, which sets up three items, requests / and asserts 3 items listed, the 'All' filter current and no message.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. A test was deleted in the final commit, so both claims are false. The 'Follow-up edits' commit message also hides the deletion.
findings.fix: Restore the test. If the deletion stays, state it in the PR body and justify it.

findings.what: The deletion left a stray blank line at the start of the 'states' describe block (line 87).
findings.fix: Remove the blank line once the test is restored.

lenses.note: The spec is present and the change follows its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. No extra behaviour was added beyond the ask. The traffic-check query allowance is needed for AC-8.
All eight acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. The state-table row 'All priorities' lost its test in the last commit.
The tests assert exact output and would fail if the code were wrong. The state test for 'All priorities' was deleted in dd38bb5. I could not run the tests here; CI covers them.
The README describes the filter. It does not mention the priority labels, but that is minor.
The SQL is parameterised, priority is validated against an allowlist, and output is HTML-escaped. No defects found beyond the stray blank line.
The priority value is checked against an allowlist before use and bound as a parameter. No injection found. The only planted-instruction concern is none.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files. QA/design review is not applicable.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the plain HTML string in src/index.js. The PR notes no browser was available.
The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is false, because the final commit deletes a test.
